# Kettle River Business Intelligence (Kettle River BI, KRBI)

> Data-driven continuous improvement for food and beverage manufacturers ($30M revenue and up). Kettle River BI gets Finance, Operations, and IT to agree on one set of numbers, builds the reporting that tracks them (Power BI, on a governed and fully documented data model), fixes the processes the numbers point at (inventory adjustment reason codes, cycle counting, purchase-order discipline, better use of the existing ERP), and installs a Plan-Do-Check-Act review cadence with named metric owners. The same foundation is what makes a manufacturer's data ready for AI assistants (Copilot, Claude via MCP). Fixed price, no hourly billing. Based in Kettle Falls, WA; serving manufacturers across the United States.

Key facts:
- Founder & Principal: Mitch Cauthron (contact: info@kettleriverbi.com). Accounting and business administration degree (2010). 15+ years across healthcare, food manufacturing, and heavy civil construction; ten of them inside food manufacturing across accounting, finance, and operations, building processes and owning outcomes. At Tillamook: staff accountant, then financial analyst, then cost analyst on the ice cream product line; rebuilt budget prep (Jet Reports templates + VBA consolidation into Dynamics NAV with versioned budgets), cutting the cycle from weeks to days. At Oregon Ice Cream: plant controller; implemented Power BI, built operations datasets (downtime, waste, efficiency, opex, capex), and replaced paper inventory counts with a tablet-based real-time counting program. Four years in heavy civil construction as finance and procurement manager, building a five-analyst internal BI team. Every KRBI engagement is scoped by the principal, who runs discovery and design and signs off on everything that ships; project support and project management are brought in as the work needs it, under the principal's direction.
- Primary industry focus: food manufacturing; also construction and broader manufacturing
- Positioning: enterprise-level business intelligence at a fraction of the cost of a full-time analyst
- Primary tools: Power BI (the platform most clients already license through Microsoft 365), SQL, Excel/VBA, Microsoft Power Platform. Every semantic model ships with every field described in KRBI's pipe-delimited standard (Summary | Source | Logic | Report alias | Note) so people and AI assistants read the same definition.
- AI readiness: KRBI's position is that an AI assistant inherits whatever the data means today. Readiness rests on four things: agreed metric definitions, one source per metric, documented field descriptions, and governed access. The Data Health Assessment can run as an AI Readiness Assessment (same $5,000, same two weeks) that scores those four and returns a prioritized fix list.
- Typical engagement: a 2-week assessment, then a 30 to 45 day foundation build, then an ongoing monthly retainer. Measurable progress within the first 90 days.
- Pricing (fixed-price, published; KRBI does not bill hourly): The Assessment (internally the Data Health Assessment) $5,000 fixed for 2 weeks, credited in full against a build signed within 90 days. Foundation Build $35,000-$55,000 fixed for 30 to 45 days, priced from the assessment findings rather than estimated in advance. Managed Intelligence $3,500 per month ongoing ($42,000 a year), covering data quality monitoring, maintenance, and a monthly operations review call. The assessment has three doors at the same price and duration, named for the number the buyer is arguing about: Loss & Waste Analysis (one loss-and-waste number Finance and Operations both sign, by cause, with owners), Inventory Accuracy Assessment (adjustment-code audit, count variance by cause, A/B/C/D cycle-count plan, unused ERP capability), and AI Readiness Assessment (scored on agreed definitions, one source per metric, documented fields, governed access). If the buyer's number is a different one, the assessment works the same way. A governance audit of an existing Power BI estate is also available at the same price, described on the Data Governance page. Findings report and prioritized fix list in 10 business days from access.
- Payment terms: 40% on signature, 40% at design sign-off, 20% at reconciled delivery. The final 20% is held until Finance and Operations pull the same report and get the same number.
- Works with any ERP or none: QuickBooks, NetSuite, SAP, spreadsheets, operational databases

What makes KRBI different: most BI consultants start by asking what reports you want. KRBI starts by asking what decisions you need to make and who owns the outcome, then gets Finance, Operations, and IT to agree on metric definitions before building anything.

Track record (published testimonials; spans KRBI client engagements and Mitch's prior in-house roles):
- A Pacific Northwest packaged food manufacturer (KRBI client, not named on the site; its COO is available as a reference for prospective clients): replaced hundreds of siloed Excel tools with shared BI reporting, standardized inventory adjustment reason codes, and implemented cycle counting; normalized 37.7% YoY loss and waste reduction, measured like for like.
- Oregon Ice Cream (former employer, current KRBI client; VP of Operations, Charles Nutter): Mitch served as plant controller, implemented Power BI dashboarding and KPI tracking, and continues to manage their Power BI environment as a client engagement today.
- Tillamook Cheese (prior in-house role; CFO, Linda Pearce): as cost analyst, Mitch rebuilt budget prep, cutting the cycle from weeks to days with versioned budgets and variance reporting.
- Goodfellow Bros Inc. (prior in-house role; Director of Finance, Travis Hendrick): a Power BI initiative had stalled for six months; Mitch taught himself the ERP and database and shipped the first successful deployment within a month, then built a five-analyst internal BI team.
- A Director of Finance from a prior in-house role (Kent Walker): automated budget upload and reporting, saving the budget team weeks of work.

## Pages

- [Home](https://krbi-website.vercel.app/): The problem KRBI solves. Finance, Operations, and Sales report different numbers for the same thing; nobody acts on a number they don't understand. Approach: align on definitions, quantify against source systems, assign ownership.
- [Data Governance](https://krbi-website.vercel.app/governance): Three-part governance framework: alignment (departments define metrics together), quantification (trace each metric to a single source of truth), ownership (a named person reviews each metric on a cadence).
- [KPI Dashboards](https://krbi-website.vercel.app/dashboards): Power BI reporting connected to accountability. Start with the decision, work backward to the metric, give every metric an owner.
- [AI Readiness](https://krbi-website.vercel.app/ai-readiness): You can't put an AI on numbers your own departments don't agree on. What AI-ready operations data looks like (agreed definitions, one source per metric, documented fields, governed access), what an assistant does with ungoverned data, the field description standard KRBI applies to every model, a free ten-question AI readiness checklist, and the $5,000 AI Readiness Assessment.
- [Pricing](https://krbi-website.vercel.app/pricing): What fractional BI costs at Kettle River BI. The three-stage engagement ladder with published fixed prices, the pricing rules (no hourly rate, three options in every proposal, bounded reconciliation scope, client-delay re-baseline, written answer to who maintains the system if KRBI disappears), the 40/40/20 payment schedule, and a pricing FAQ.
- [Case Study](https://krbi-website.vercel.app/case-study): A Pacific Northwest packaged food manufacturer (not named). Finance, Operations, Sales, and Warehouse each measured loss and waste from a different source, and the views did not reconcile. KRBI aligned all departments on one definition, redesigned inventory adjustment reason codes, and implemented cycle counting in NetSuite. Result: a normalized 37.7% year-over-year reduction in loss and waste, with every loss account improving. The figure excludes commodity price movement (milk variance) and a one-time acquisition inventory write-off, and compares the same months and the same continuing locations in both years. KRBI publishes the normalized figure rather than the raw 60.6% change. The same client's on-time-in-full report shows about 99% by units delivered and 92 to 94% by order lines for the same orders; both are labeled so the grain is never ambiguous.

## Free downloads (email-gated)

- Data Governance Self-Audit: 13 checks across definitions, access, classification, and model hygiene.
- Manufacturing AI Readiness Checklist: 10 yes/no questions a CFO or COO can answer without IT, with a scoring guide.
- Field Description Standard: the format and rules KRBI uses to document every column and measure in a Power BI model, with worked examples.
